propositions: Janitor discovery concern #12 must be added to systematically detect when test assertions cannot fail on contract violations, proven by concrete escape inputs that pass the oracle but violate the contract.

The oracle-strength rubric exists only in code-review-tests.md and runs only on diffs; concern #12 must extend it to the full resting test tree by defining a portable schema with contract, oracle, escape_input, antipattern_id, and scope fields.

discovery.md hardcodes 'eleven concerns' in its output schema while defining only eleven numbered concerns; adding concern #12 without updating the schema creates a silent disagreement that nothing fails to catch, so an executable test must derive and assert the count from both sides.

verification.md must anchor the production-impact floor on the guarded contract rather than the test file location, and require tree-state evidence (a broken stub or reasoned escape_input) to prove harm is reachable, else reclassify weak-oracle findings as hardening.

The portable antipattern vocabulary for concern #12 must include the three classes verified absent from code-review-tests.md: fixture-mutates-foreign-state, mismatched-hardening-equivalence, and unstated-policy-oracle, enabling janitor to run on non-rebar repos lacking the code-review-tests.md rubric.
